https://www.dw.com/en/russia-top-court-b.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Iaqy 'Everything we do,' said Yabloko leader Nikolai Rybakov, should be dedicated to 'stopping deaths and bringing back peace' Image: Yevgeny Messman/TASS/picture alliance Advertisement The Supreme Court of Russia on Monday ruled in favor of the nationalist pro-Kremlin Rodina (Motherland) party and barred Yabloko (Apple) — Russia's only anti-war party — from participating in September parliamentary elections. Rodina accuses Yabloko of receiving undeclared financial support from Western sources, among other things. Arguing before the court, Yabloko vehemently denied the accusations and railed against Rodina's lack of supporting evidence. The nationalist pro-Kremlin Rodina party brought the case, accusing Yabloko of receiving foreign funding, yet without providing evidence to support the claim Image: Pavel Seleznev/TASS/picture alliance On Monday, Judge Vyacheslav Kirillov said, "The claims seeking to annul the registration of the federal list of candidates for the State Duma of the ninth convocation, nominated by the Yabloko political party, were granted." The court's decision means citizens opposed to Russia's four-and-a-half-year invasion of Ukraine — or "special military operation" as it has been legally deemed under penalty of imprisonment — have no opportunity to vote for representatives willing to articulate that opposition. Yabloko leader Nikolay Rybakov told the hundred or so supporters gathered outside the court, "Excluding Yabloko from the election means refusing dialog with people who ask questions that are uncomfortable for the authorities." "We have a long road ahead and we have a big and important task — to stop deaths and bring back peace. Everything we do should be dedicated to that," Rybakov added, vowing to appeal the decision. Yabloko — the only liberal party still operating in Russia since most of President Vladimir Putin 's opponents have been jailed, exiled or murdered — has received the backing of several exiled opposition figures, including Yulia Navalnaya , the widow of the late opposition leader Alexei Navalny . Yabloko was once a strong liberal force in Russia but like other opposition outfits it has been systematically sidelined by the Kremlin. The party is currently only polling around three percent — short of the five percent threshold for entry into parliament — and has not won a seat in the federal State Duma since 2003. Putin-backing United Russia has won every single election since then and that is expected to again be the case in September. Yabloko supporters ignored the threat of repression to show support for the party's anti-war stance at the Supreme Court Image: Yevgeny Messman/TASS/picture alliance But despite barring political opposition to the war, public opinion toward the conflict has soured, more so since Ukraine has intensified its attacks on energy and logistics infrastructure inside Russia. The non-governmental Levada Center — which is on the Kremlin's "foreign agents" list — charts support at around 66%, the lowest since Russia launched its attack against neighboring Ukraine on February 24, 2022. The Kremlin has cracked down on opposition to the war with strict censorship rules and mass arrests, with many activists and journalists preferring to flee than to face potentially deadly persecution by staying in Russia . https://www.politico.eu/article/nigel-fa.text: BIRMINGHAM, England — France’s Jordan Bardella and Britain’s Nigel Farage on Friday staged a grand display of anti-immigration, populist kinship in their first joint appearance Reform UK’s annual conference on Friday. But their plan to end migrant crossings in the English Channel, which was formalized with their signatures on an oversized memorandum of understanding, did not definitively settle the thorniest issue when it comes to any migration agreement: Whether France will take back migrants who are captured trying to enter United Kingdom after leaving French shores on so-called small boats. Farage in August announced that if he wins power, he would use the Royal Navy to launch the “largest military operation in the English Channel since World War II” to intercept so-called small boats and return migrants to French shores, triggering an uproar in France. Advertisement Advertisement The document Farage and Bardella signed is only binding if the two parties come to power, and it says France will “will ordinarily accept” migrants intercepted in the Channel — potentially leaving wiggle room for Paris to reject them in some cases. Farage called the line “legalese” at a press conference alongside Bardella. “As Australia proved in 2012, once you provide no incentive to pay a trafficker money to be taken across a stretch of water, in very very short order, the business model will be broken,” Farage said. But Farage was not asked about the fact that the phrase does not even appear in the French version of the agreement. A National Rally official, granted anonymity to discuss the agreement’s finer points, said the French translation is the “final” version of the agreement. The memorandum in both languages says the French will be responsible for deporting migrants to their countries of origin, and that the costs of policing operations will be assessed later. It adds that that France will do “its upmost” to stop departures. “If France gains control of its borders there will be no departures [from French shores],” Bardella said in a speech at the conference. “If we end up doing pushbacks, it would be a failure of our government, it would mean that we have let dozens of thousands of people enter France illegally,” he added. And the National Rally has long vowed to submit its immigration plans to a referendum in France, which is a lengthy and uncertain process that could get derailed even Bardella’s mentor, Marine Le Pen, wins the presidential election next year. Polls have consistently showed she is the front-runner. Advertisement Advertisement Still, Farage, whose marquee event was overshadowed by illegal party funding allegations that emerged Thursday , likened the pact to “a genuine new Entente Cordiale.” In a 20-minute address delivered in English, Bardella pledged to work hand in hand with a Reform government if Le Pen wins to stop flows of illegal migration into the United Kingdom. Bardella also indicated that the returns across the Channel would be unlikely to be implemented because France would stop all illegal immigration if they came to power. “Our government will do everything in its power to ensure that France is no longer the gateway for illegal migration into the United Kingdom,” Bardella said.
